title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A row missing from the checklist's template while the record still writes it: the two a person pastes side by side would no longer match.

title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A field the workflow computes and the record does not list: applyPrior drops it silently and the run's issue never shows whether the attestation was verified.

find: | Previous version installed | (step 22: the version installed before this one, 0.1.0; none where step 22 was not run) |
title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: The update's field gone from the checklist's template while the record still writes it: a person run would not say which version it updated over.

title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A field the template has and the record does not list: the automated run's record would lack the row that says the update was not automated.

title: is the results template, row for row
why: Step 22 gone from the template's steps while the record still writes its row: the update over 0.1.0 would have nowhere to be recorded by a person.

title: names every step as its heading does, the time left blank there
why: Step 22 missing from the record: the automated run could not say it is not automated, and the record would claim twenty-one steps where the checklist has twenty-two.

title: answers from the tag's own file, true where it holds the text and false where not
why: Every tag that has the file read as holding the feature: a release from before the label is expected to report its -rc.N, and fails a row it passes.

title: answers null without a tag, for a tag this clone lacks, and without git
why: A tag the clone does not have read as one without the feature, so the App row is judged by the older rule instead of recorded as not checked.

title: answers false for a tag whose tree has no such file, and asks for no text
why: git's "no such path" read as git failing: a tag from before the file is recorded as not checked instead of judged by the older rule.

title: answers null when reading the file fails or times out, whatever it printed
why: A read that failed or timed out taken as the file: the tag is judged as one without the feature, on what git never finished printing.

title: adds up to the time it says the sitting takes
why: An item's minutes changed and the sitting's stated length not: the person is told 45 minutes for a sitting of 46.

find:
### 10. The versions and the verdict

**3 minutes.**
replace:
### 10. The versions and the verdict

3 minutes.
title: has ten items, numbered in order, each opening on its minutes
why: An item with no minutes line: its time drops out of the total silently, and the sum still looks whole.

find: | 10 | The versions and the verdict | fine / finding | |
title: has a results form with a row for each item, by its title
why: The verdict's row gone from the results form: the sitting's issue would have nowhere to say go or no-go.

title: links only to headings that are there
why: A link from the sitting to a heading that is not there: GitHub opens the top of the page and the person is left to find the section.

title: has no pending heading that has landed
why: A heading allowed to be missing has landed and its entry stays: a later rename of it would break the links to it unseen.

title: links only to headings that are there
why: A link inside the accessibility record to a heading that is not there: the person walking it is sent to the top of a long page.

title: refuses both, with a sentence
why: Both given and the dispatch carries on: a tag's Release and a build run mixed in one record.

title: refuses neither, with a sentence
why: Neither given and the dispatch carries on with nothing to accept.

title: refuses a run of another workflow, by id and not by name
why: Any run's artefacts accepted as a build's.

title: refuses a run with a package job that did not succeed, naming it
why: A build with a failed package job rehearsed as though it had installers.

title: is refused where a candidate's record is required, and a candidate's is let through
why: A rehearsal's record counted as a candidate's run of the gate.

title: heads a rehearsal record as one, with its run and commit, and a candidate record plainly
why: A rehearsal's record that does not say so.

title: leaves the tag's step 1, with its checksum and attestation, to a tag alone
why: The Release's checksum and attestation check run, and fail, on a rehearsal that has no Release.

title: refuses spaces around either input, rather than trimming what the workflow uses as given
why: A padded input trimmed in the check but used as given by the workflow: both checkouts or a wrong run id.

title: keys both checkouts of at-tag on the dispatch result, never on the raw inputs
why: A padded run input alongside a tag runs both checkouts, the second with an empty ref.

title: reads a record with Windows line ends the same
why: A CRLF rehearsal record read as unknown and let past nothing, or a candidate's misjudged.

title: says the version a build reports: X.Y.Z+<sha7> for main or a branch, the tag for a tag push
why: A tag-push build expected to report X.Y.Z+sha7 and failed on the right version.

title: names a tag push by its tag, and a branch that looks like one by its branch
why: A tag push judged as a branch build.

find: echo "- Attestation verified? not verified (a rehearsal; no attestation)"

why: A rehearsal's reader summary says the app it walked was attested, which nothing checked.

why: A rehearsal writes VoiceOver clauses naming the app's version and a run, ready to be committed to the record as though a candidate had been heard.

title: never records a rehearsal's step 1 as a pass, nor its checksum or attestation as yes
why: A rehearsal's step 1 recorded as passed, though it checked neither the checksum nor the attestation a tagged run's step 1 is passed on.

title: never records a rehearsal's step 1 as a pass, nor its checksum or attestation as yes
why: A rehearsal's record says its installer's attestation was verified, when there was none to verify.

title: makes step 22's update with the build run's own installer
why: Steps 2 and 22 look for a Release's file name that a rehearsal never downloaded, and step 22 installs nothing over 0.1.0.
